Lalmohan Babu.description: A popular thriller writer and close friend of Feluda who often accompanies him on investigations.

Feluda.description: A renowned private investigator from Calcutta and the protagonist of the series, also known as Feluda.

Jayant Biswas.description: A fellow traveler on the train to Lucknow, a Christian whose family has lived in Lucknow for generations. He is married to Shakuntala Devi's daughter.

Shakuntala Devi.description: A famous silent film actress, originally named Virginia Reynolds, and the mother-in-law of Jayant Biswas.

Jaisalmer.description: A historic city in Rajasthan, India, known for its golden sandstone fort.

Lucknow.description: The capital city of Uttar Pradesh, India, famous for its history, culture, and Mughal heritage.

Gangtok.description: The capital of Sikkim, a state in northeastern India.

Aurangzeb.description: A Mughal emperor who ruled India in the 17th century.

Mughal.description: Refers to the Mughal dynasty, which ruled large parts of India from the 16th to 19th centuries.

nawabs.description: Nawab is a title for a Muslim nobleman or ruler in South Asia; nawabs is the plural form, referring to such rulers, especially in northern India during the Mughal era.

mutiny of 1857.description: A major uprising against British rule in India, also known as the First War of Independence.

Calcutta.description: Now called Kolkata, a major city in eastern India and Feluda's home.

Doon Express.description: A long-distance train in India connecting Howrah (Kolkata) to Dehradun, passing through Lucknow.

Howrah.description: A major railway station and city adjacent to Kolkata.

Avadh.description: The Urdu name for the historical region of Oudh, of which Lucknow is the capital.

Ayodhya.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, considered an ancient and holy city in Hindu tradition.

Laxman.description: A figure from the Hindu epic Ramayana, brother of Lord Rama; the name 'Lucknow' is said to derive from him.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic narrating the life of Lord Rama.

Gomti.description: A river that flows through Lucknow.

Bengali Club.description: A social club for Bengalis living in Lucknow.

Shaken in Shanghai.description: A book written by Lalmohan Babu (Jatayu).

Japan.description: A country in East Asia, mentioned as the origin of Lalmohan Babu's suitcase.

H J B.description: The initials on Jayant Biswas's suitcase, standing for Hector Jayant Biswas.

Bioscope.description: A magazine about films, popular during the era of silent movies.

Anglo-Indian.description: A term for people of mixed Indian and British ancestry.

Thomas Reynolds.description: Father of Virginia Reynolds, served in the army and spoke Urdu.

Urdu.description: A language widely spoken in northern India and Pakistan.

Maharaja of Mysore.description: A royal title; the ruler of Mysore, a princely state in southern India.

Mysore.description: A city and former princely state in southern India.

Badshah Bagh.description: A locality in Lucknow, where Jayant Biswas lives.

Mughlai.description: A style of cuisine developed in the kitchens of the Mughal Empire, known for its rich flavors.

Puja.description: Puja, short for Durga Puja, is a major Hindu festival celebrating the goddess Durga, especially important to Bengalis.

berths.description: Sleeping compartments or beds in a train coach.

talkie.description: A term for a film with sound, as opposed to a silent film.

Goan.description: Goan refers to a person from Goa, a state on the western coast of India, while Goans is the plural form, often associated with music and Western culture.

waistcoat.description: A sleeveless upper-body garment, often worn over a shirt and under a jacket.

film buff.description: A person who is very interested in and knowledgeable about films.

Mr Biswas.description: A passenger on the Doon Express, he is married to Pamela Suneela and is involved in the business of imports and exports.

Mr Sukius.description: A well-known businessman from Lucknow and an art connoisseur who was murdered during the course of the investigation.

Farida Begum.description: A kathak dancer who married Thomas Reynolds and became Virginia's mother.

Edward.description: Son of Thomas Reynolds and Farida Begum, became a lawyer.

Charles.description: Son of Thomas Reynolds and Farida Begum, managed a tea estate in Assam.

Percival Motilal Banerjee.description: Virginia's husband, a Bengali Christian and film producer who encouraged her acting career.

Margaret Susheela.description: The elder sister of Suneela Biswas and daughter of Virginia and Percival; she is married to Samuel Saldanha.

Victor Prasenjit.description: The son of Mr and Mrs Biswas.

Mary Sheela.description: The daughter of Mr and Mrs Biswas who is an aspiring journalist and decorator.

Buxar.description: A town in Bihar, India, mentioned as a stop on the train journey.

Mughalsarai.description: A major railway junction in Uttar Pradesh, India.

Pratapgarh.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, another stop on the train route.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, from where Lalmohan Babu's razors were brought.

Wilkinson.description: A brand of razor blades, known for their quality.

New Market.description: A famous shopping area in Kolkata, India.

Bengal regiment.description: A historical British Indian Army regiment.

Assam.description: A state in northeastern India, known for its tea estates.

bearer.description: A servant or attendant, especially on trains in India.

hookah.description: A traditional Indian water pipe used for smoking tobacco.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

attar.description: A fragrant essential oil derived from botanical sources, used as perfume.

nawab.description: A title for a Muslim nobleman or ruler in South Asia.

kathak.description: A classical dance form from northern India.

Babu.description: A respectful term for a gentleman or educated man in India.

Dr Srivastava.description: A character mentioned in connection with a previous adventure in Lucknow.

Bonobihari Babu.description: Owner of an amazing zoo, referenced from a previous visit.

Mr Saldanha.description: A Goan owner of a musical instrument shop in Lucknow who is married to Margaret Susheela.

Albert Ratanlal Banerjee.description: Albert Ratanlal Banerjee is Mrs Biswas's brother and Jayant Biswas's brother-in-law, described as having lighter skin and eyes. He is sometimes referred to as Mr Banerjee or simply Ratanlal.

Suleman.description: The long-serving bearer (servant) of the Biswas family, who has been with them for thirty years.

Emperor Aurangzeb.description: A Mughal emperor of India, referenced in connection with a diamond ring from a previous adventure.

Haridwar.description: A holy city in Uttarakhand, India, known for its religious significance.

Laxmanjhoola.description: A famous suspension bridge in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, India.

Bara Imambara.description: A grand historical monument in Lucknow, famous for its large hall and architectural marvel.

Bhulbhulaiya.description: The labyrinth or maze within the Bara Imambara complex in Lucknow.

begums.description: A term for noblewomen or wives of nawabs in India.

The Residency.description: A historical site in Lucknow, significant for its role during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

sepoys.description: Indian soldiers, especially those who served under British command during colonial times.

bhoona peda.description: A type of sweetmeat for which Lucknow is famous.

Chhota Imambara.description: Another important historical monument in Lucknow.

Chattar Manzil.description: A palace in Lucknow, also known as the 'Umbrella Palace.'

Hazratganj.description: A prominent shopping area in Lucknow.

sitars.description: A traditional Indian stringed musical instrument.

maharajas.description: Indian kings or princes, especially those who ruled princely states.

Imambara.description: A congregation hall for Shia Muslim commemoration ceremonies, especially during Muharram.

peda.description: A type of Indian sweet, usually made from khoya (reduced milk) and sugar.

bungalow.description: A single-storied house, commonly found in India.

ma.description: A Hindi and Bengali word meaning 'mother.'

paanwala.description: A paanwala is a person who sells paan, a popular Indian chew made of betel leaf and areca nut; paanwalas is the plural form.

Inspector Pandey.description: Inspector Pandey is the police officer in charge of investigating the theft of Shakuntala's necklace, assisting Feluda with the case.

Mrs Biswas.description: The wife of Mr Biswas and mother of the Biswas children; she is the owner of the stolen necklace and sister to Albert Ratanlal Banerjee.

Mr Som.description: A well-known portrait painter who lives with the Biswas family after his retirement.

Clive Road.description: A street or locality where Mr and Mrs Saldanha live.

Kaizer Bagh.description: A notable historical site or garden in Lucknow, mentioned as a sightseeing destination.

Tribhuvan Nagar.description: Mr Biswas's business partner in Modern Imports & Exports.

Pioneer.description: A publication that wrote a biography mentioning the necklace.

Modern Imports & Exports.description: The business firm run by Mr Biswas and his partner.

Frazer Road.description: A street where Ratanlal, Mr Biswas's brother-in-law, lives.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar, often associated with South Asia.

salwar-kameez.description: A traditional outfit worn by women in South Asia, consisting of a tunic (kameez) and trousers (salwar).

Pamela.description: Margaret's younger sister, recipient of the stolen necklace and considered more talented and favored by their mother.

Saldanha & Co..description: An old music shop in Hazratganj, Lucknow, run by the Saldanha family.

de Mello.description: Owner of one of the other music shops in Lucknow, identified as Goan.

Noronha.description: Owner of another music shop in Lucknow, also identified as Goan.

America.description: Refers to the United States, where Mr Saldanha's son lives and works.

Kulu.description: A region in Himachal Pradesh, India, known for its apple orchards.

ghazals.description: A poetic form and genre of music originating in Arabic poetry, popular in India and often set to music.

hi-fi.description: Short for 'high fidelity', refers to high-quality sound reproduction equipment.

objets d’art.description: French term meaning 'art objects', used in India to refer to decorative or collectible art pieces.

Dilkhusha.description: Dilkhusha is a historical building, once a pleasure palace, now in ruins, located in Lucknow.

Nawab Sadat Ali.description: Nawab Sadat Ali was a ruler in Lucknow who commissioned the construction of Dilkhusha in the nineteenth century.

La Martiniere School.description: La Martiniere School is a famous educational institution in Lucknow, established in the eighteenth century.

Claude Martin.description: Claude Martin was a Major General who founded La Martiniere School in the eighteenth century.

tonga.description: A horse-drawn carriage commonly used for local transport in parts of India.

chamchas.description: A Hindi slang term meaning 'sycophants' or 'cronies', often used derogatorily.

Biswas.description: A surname referring to the 'Biswas boy,' a suspect in another case mentioned in the chapter.

goonda.description: A Hindi/Bengali term for a hired thug or criminal.

Topshe.description: Feluda's cousin, loyal assistant, and the narrator of the stories.

Shambhu Singh.description: A hired killer who confesses to the murder of Mr Sukius and identifies his employer.

Kanpur.description: A city in northern India, mentioned as Mr Sukius's intended destination.

Saldanhas.description: A family involved in the story, with members present during the investigation.
